recipes.name: Slow Cooker Latin Chicken
ingredients_raw: salt and ground black pepper to taste
0.5 cup fresh cilantro, coarsely chopped, divided
2 (15.5 ounce) cans black beans, rinsed and drained
2 large sweet potatoes, cut into chunks
1 red bell pepper, cut into strips

steps.text: Heat olive oil in a large skillet. Season chicken with salt and pepper; sprinkle 1/4 cup cilantro over chicken thighs. Cook chicken in hot oil until browned, 3 to 5 minutes per side. Arrange chicken in the bottom of a slow cooker.
Place black beans, sweet potatoes, and red bell pepper on top of chicken. Mix together salsa, chicken broth, 1/4 cup cilantro, garlic, cumin, and allspice in a bowl; pour into the slow cooker.
Cook on Low for 4 hours. Garnish with lime wedges to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Slow Cooker Latin Chicken
raw_recipe.description: Spicy cumin, chicken, salsa, black beans, and sweet potatoes combine into a flavorful Latin chicken stew. The thigh meat has unbelievable flavor and tenderness.

review.reviewBody: I really think people should take note to the user who doubled her sauce. I only used 1 package (2lb) of boneless thighs (bone-in works fine though!) and 1.5 sweet potatoes, and the tops were burning and black beans dried out because it was not covered in liquid. So, I doubled the cumin, allspice, garlic, 1.5C salsa (light, med, hot doesn't matter), and 2/3C broth. Use a slotted spoon if you don't want soupy, but this really wasn't! Used box of uncle ben's chicken wild rice (with the seasoning) to serve on top of, and people go ga-ga over all the flavor. This definitely makes the house smell warm. We "HATE" sweet potatoes, so my husband cringed when I told him what this was made of, yet this is now both of our favorite meals. I'm so glad I trusted the reviews. Also added a can of corn, and glad I did as it was the perfect mix of flavors!

Made mine in a Dutch Oven with Crispy Skin Thighs! It was so good. I deboned my 5 big thighs - 1st time super easy - run a sharp knife on the underside right next to the bone, not cutting all the way thru - sooo easy! And then trim out the cartlidge at the end. Voila. Didn't have hot salsa so used medium Picante sauce (thicker salsa for cooking medium and sprinkled one side of the thighs with cayenne. and no pepper/ Used my enameled Lodge Dutch Oven, browned both sides a little longer to get the cooking started more - removed, then added garlic, sauteed few mins. then add all other ingredients. As others suggested used one can black beans and 1 cup of corn. Darn my cilantro had gone bad so I used parsley and sprinkled in corriander (ground cilantro seed) in place. Used at least 1 cup + broth and probably double the pcante sauce/salsa - didn't measure but there was a lot to cover in pot - Placed thighs on top, skin side up and cooked in oven at about 375- 400 for 1-1/2 hrs maybe a little more - removed the lid last few minute to crisp up the skin which was already nicely browned anyway. This was so different and delicious -The sweet potatoes absorbed the heat from the cayenne - it had a nice "gravy" and served it over brown rice. Hearty, healthy, filling meal - the chicken was super!

This is the second time I've made this recipe. The first time, I followed the recipe almost exactly -- mild salsa, and no cilantro because it tastes like soap, LOL! It could have used a bit more liquid; there wasn't much with which to moisten rice. This time, I used the last of the leftover Thanksgiving turkey (already cooked) from the freezer instead of chicken; a can of kidney beans and a cup of garbanzo beans, because I had no black beans (surprise!); and mild salsa and no cilantro. Since the cooked turkey had no juices to release, I added an additional cup of water, which really made a difference. Both times I've made this recipe, I've thrown everything into the Instant Pot on "stew" setting, and manually released pressure as soon as it was done, so the sweet potatoes don't turn to mush. It's aromatic, delicious, and satisfying!

I skipped the browning step and used 2 cups of salsa, and 3/4 cup broth, and extra cumin. I also added some frozen corn. We didn't think the pepper added anything so I'd leave that out next time. Served over rice.

This recipe is awesome!!! I have made it for years after finding it here on Allrecipes. I fixed it last week for friends & family. All went home with the recipe! I made it in the instant pot for the first time. It worked great! Sauteed in pot. Add everything else . Put the lid on & set it for stew. In 35 minutes it will be done to perfection.

We did change this up some, but even my elderly mom loves this recipe! Just adjust the heat. I added some chopped celery and onions, used chopped yellow pepper, black beans, 2 C salsa, 1 C broth, and doubled the spices with a little added chili powder and garlic n onion powder (not salt) to the liquid mix. I always brown the chicken as I feel it adds a depth you don't get otherwise. Sometimes I even sprinkle Chix with a little flour then brown. Helps thicken sauce if you have to cook longer so more broth to keep moist. We have used butternut squash rather than sweet potatoes and it's just as good! If u have a time crunch, brown the chix more thoroughly, and put slow cooker on high for 1st 30 min to get everything hot, then turn down to low and it won't take 4 hrs, but still good.

I made this the other night for dinner. I followed to suggestion to use a bit more salsa and chicken broth so it wouldn't dry out. Cooked on high for about 3 hours and another hour on low. When I stirred it the chicken simply shredded and the chunks of sweet potatoes disappeared (which was a good thing). I served it over steamed rice. The GF and and I ate it. It was good. Last night I used it as taco filling in crunchy taco shells with shredded lettuce and cheese and tomatoes. Those were a big hit. Even the extremely picky 11 years old liked them. Neither of them knew about the sweet potatoes. Well hidden, I guess. Tonight I'm going to use it for enchilada filling. So much leftovers from just one recipe.

UPDATE: So I made the enchiladas. I used the sauce recipe from The Pioneer Woman's 'Enchiladas' recipe. (She has several enchilada recipes. I used the one simply name 'Enchiladas'.) The change I made to her recipe was to use a 19oz can of red enchilada sauce and a 10oz can of green enchilada sauce (instead of using a 28oz can of only one kind). I dipped the fried corn tortillas in the sauce. Put a bit the the mixture from this recipe in the tortillas with a little cheese. Filled to baking dishes. Topped with more cheese and the remainder of the sauce. Baked at 350F for 30 minutes. We can't stop talking about how good they are.

It seemed easy and tasty and everything was on hand except chicken and cilantro, which were purchased yesterday.
Prefer thighs rather than breasts, as they have more flavor. What I bought were six thighs, bone in, skin on. Prior to serving removed the skin. Followed the recipe with a couple of changes, mainly the addition of turmeric which I tend to add to every stew or soup, and I always prefer to use jarred roasted red peppers for the ease and flavor. We also prefer medium salsa. What seemed odd to me was setting the crock pot on low for four hours. Normally it's high for four and low for eight. Fortunately I was at home during this cooking process today and while it was initially set on low, noticed after two hours that the potato chunks were still hard as rocks, so changed it to high for the remaining two hours. Also felt the need to add more liquid, as others have stated. Ended up with nearly 2 cups of chicken broth, rather than the initial half cup. Not sure if the temperature was a misprint or not, but thankful I was at home to check and not assume that the meal would be done on low in four hours. 
The two of us enjoyed the meal with bread, salad and wine . There are definitely enough leftovers for one more meal. This is a keeper for us and so it shall be made again.
Thanks to the person who sent it in.

We really liked this - made as written except only 1 tsp of cumin and my black beans were 19oz cans - could have used more broth. I did brown the chicken and assembled everything into the crockpot the night before then put in the fridge - turned it on at noon the next day so it was ready for supper. After 4 1/2 hours on low I turned it up to high for an hour when I got home from work as potatoes were not cooked but the extra time on high fixed that. Overall a nice change for supper and will make it again but with more juice next time.

Didn't have time for slow cooker so did it on stove top. Added a small chopped onion, just one can of beans and one and half cups of frozen corn, upped the broth to 1 cup. Used 1 tsp cumin and 3 tsp. taco seasoning mix. Lightly coated the chicken thighs in flour then browned, added peppers and onion cooked for few minutes then added everything else and simmered for 1 hour. I substituted red potatoes for the sweet as that was what I had. Very good!

If you “don’t like chicken thighs,” you should try this dish! I basically never write reviews, but this was so tasty I felt compelled to review it! I also don’t typically use chicken thighs but I trusted the recipe and the chicken was soooo flavorful and tender! I made it exactly as listed. Based on other reviews, I cut the sweet potatoes in very large chunks (basically 2” rounds, keeping the skin intact around each piece) so they wouldn’t disintegrate. At the very end, I removed the sweet potatoes to a plate and added a small amount of dried potato flakes (my trick for thickening sauces) to the slow cooker and let the sauce thicken for about 10 more minutes. So delicious and easy; I’ll be making this again soon!
Very healthty and flaovorful!!
THIS IS FIRE!!!! My family loves it I've been making this for probably 10 yrs now
loved this. I didnt have fresh cilantro so I used about 2 t . of dried. also used a can of ro-tel tomatoes in place of salsa. so good!
Great FLavors and easy to make. I had to add more CHX broth than called for and raise the temp to high for an hour because it didn't cover and cook the sweet potato well. I will make again.
no it was amazing as is..I've already been back for seconds and thirds,but it"s so good I can't help myself!! ONLY in El Salvador you can get this homemade AMAZING FOOD..
Very tasty my wife and I both loved it
Delicious! I always in crease the amount of spices.
Tasted great! I did not have black beans so I used kidney beans and pigeon peas and it was delicious! I also used drumsticks instead of thighs.

I used skinless chicken breast cut up into small pieces and didn’t brown ( I require a very low fat diet) and used 1 1/2 c broth. I had only medium salsa so I added red pepper flakes to add personal taste of spice/heat. My slow cooker is older & maybe VERY slow & I found sweet potato not soft even at 6 hours so cooked longer. I used the 1 can corn 1 can beans as well. I added a teaspoon of salt part way through cooking just finding it bland but I think one can do this to your own taste. We are over a mix of wild and basmati rice.
